title: Your revenue is smaller than you think

script.title: Your revenue is smaller than you think
script.summary: VAT for travel agents, the ₦5 million penalty for using unregistered contractors, company versus business name, and how to clear a VAT backlog.

personas.name: Funke
personas.role: Runs a travel agency in Lekki

lines.speaker: p-funke
lines.text: If I add 7.5% VAT to a ₦3 million package, nobody will book it. Abeg, do I still have to pay VAT to government?

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Welcome to The Bridge, from TaxStreem. Every Friday, business owners bring their tax questions to our virtual open office, and on this show we replay the best ones.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Before we start, a quick note. The voices you're hearing are AI-generated. The answers come from Kelechi Ibe, TaxStreem's co-founder and a licensed tax practitioner, from last Friday's session. We've changed names and details to protect the people who asked.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Today we cover VAT for travel agents, a ₦5 million mistake procurement teams keep making, and whether a company really pays less tax than a business name.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Our first voice note is from Funke. She runs a small travel agency in Lekki.

lines.speaker: p-funke
lines.text: Good afternoon. Business is tough right now, and everybody is cutting prices. If a package to Zanzibar costs ₦3 million and I add 7.5% VAT on top, nobody will book it. Abeg, if I don't collect VAT from my customer, do I still have to pay VAT to government?

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Thank you, Funke. This is exactly the kind of question we started these sessions for. Let me take it in two parts.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: First, whether you should be charging VAT at all. Under the Nigeria Tax Act, which took effect on the first of January 2026, a small business doesn't have to register for VAT, charge it, or file VAT returns. Small means your turnover for the year is ₦100 million or less, and your fixed assets are not more than 250 million. Until last year the line was 25 million, so the threshold has quadrupled.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: There's one exception. If you provide professional services, say you're a lawyer or an accountant, you don't count as a small business at all. You comply with VAT whatever your turnover.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Now the second part, and this is where I see travel agencies make mistakes. Your revenue is not the ₦3 million. The airline flies your customer and the hotel gives them a room. Your job is to connect the parties, and what you earn for that is your commission. Under IFRS 15, an agent recognises only that commission as revenue.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: So if your fee on that package is 10%, your revenue is ₦300,000. That changes two things. You're far less likely to cross the 100 million threshold in the first place. And once you do cross it, your VAT sits on your service fee alone. The airline and the hotel account for tax on their own part of the package.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: 7.5% of 300,000 is ₦22,500. On the full package, you would have charged 225,000. Your customer will hardly notice the smaller figure.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: One warning, though. If you've already collected VAT from a customer, please pay it over. That money belongs to government, and if they come for it, you'll pay it back with interest and penalties.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Kelechi added one more point for anyone sitting below the threshold.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: You can still choose to charge VAT, and sometimes you should. Every time you buy a laptop, pay a consultant or fix the office generator, you pay VAT. That's your input VAT. When you charge VAT on your own sales, you deduct your input VAT and pay government only the difference.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Say in October you collect ₦1 million of VAT from customers and pay 500,000 on purchases. You remit 500,000. If you don't charge VAT at all, that 500,000 is just a cost that eats into your profit. And when your input VAT is bigger than your output VAT, government owes you the difference, and you can claim it back.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Next, a voice note from Chinedu, who manages facilities for a manufacturing company in Ota.

lines.speaker: p-chinedu
lines.text: Good evening sir. The best AC repair man we know runs a one-man shop. No CAC, no registration, nothing. He's cheaper than the big service companies, and his work is better. With this new tax law, can we keep using him if we just self-charge the VAT on his invoices?

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Chinedu, I understand why you want to keep him. Self-charge solves a VAT problem, and your problem here is registration. Those are two different things.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: The Tax Administration Act says a company or statutory body that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦5 million. Self-charging the VAT does nothing about that penalty.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: The fix is cheap. Ask him to register a business name with CAC. Once he does, he gets a Tax ID automatically, with no separate tax registration. Then you can keep giving him jobs at the same good price, and nobody is exposed.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Funke came back with a second question.

lines.speaker: p-funke
lines.text: Thank you sir, that one has cleared my head. My business is registered as a business name, and we've been trying to convert to a limited company. Everybody says a company pays less tax. Is it true?

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: It depends on your numbers. A small company pays zero company income tax. But the money in the company is not your money. You still have to take it out, either as a salary, which is taxed as your personal income, or as dividends.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Let's use one example. Your turnover is just under 100 million, and your profit for the year is ₦60 million.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: As a small company, you pay no company income tax. You declare the 60 million as a dividend, the company deducts 10% withholding tax, which is ₦6 million, and that's the end of it. Run the same business as a business name, and the 60 million is taxed as your personal income on the new tax bands. Before any reliefs, that comes to about ₦12.9 million. So the company route saves you close to 7 million.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Now watch what happens once your turnover crosses 100 million. The company pays 30% income tax plus a 4% development levy, and you still deduct 10% on the dividend. On the same 60 million profit, that's over ₦24 million in tax. At that size, the business name comes out cheaper.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: And on cost, a small company doesn't need an external audit to file. A simple statement of profit and loss will do. So running a small company is cheaper than most people think.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Our last question came in writing before the session. It says: our VAT has been piling up for a while, and we're finally ready to face it. Where do we start?

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Start by finding out what you actually owe. Get a consultant to work it out properly. Many businesses think they're sitting on a huge liability, and when you do the numbers, most of it turns out to be late filing penalties.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: If the amount is manageable, clear it and start on a clean slate. If it isn't, start complying from today, so the problem stops growing. And file this year's returns now. On Rev360, penalties and interest are calculated automatically the moment a return is late, and no tax officer can negotiate them away.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: If the tax office later sends you an assessment, a consultant can engage them on it. Negotiating an assessment through the proper process is legal. Paying a bribe to make it disappear is not, and I won't support that.

lines.speaker: ch-kelechi
lines.text: Here's why it matters. On Rev360, you cannot download a tax clearance certificate while any return is outstanding. I once had a client who needed his TCC within a week to get his fitness products onto the shelves of a big gym chain. Today there's no shortcut for that. If your filings aren't complete, the certificate won't come out, and the deal goes to whoever was ready.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: That's the show. Every Friday at 4 p.m., TaxStreem runs a free virtual open office where you can bring your own tax questions. The link to register is in the description, and you can send your questions ahead of time.

lines.speaker: ch-ada
lines.text: Every business is different, so treat today's answers as a starting point and speak to an adviser about your own situation. I'm Ada. See you next Friday on The Bridge.

polls.question: Say Funke is above the threshold. What should she charge VAT on?
polls.why: As an agent, her revenue is her commission. The airline and hotel handle tax on their own part.

polls.question: Does self-charging VAT protect Chinedu's company from the penalty?
options: No, the penalty is about registration
polls.why: Self-charge deals with VAT. The ₦5m penalty is for contracting someone with no registration.

polls.question: Turnover just under ₦100m, profit ₦60m. Which structure pays less tax?
polls.why: ₦6m in dividend withholding tax against about ₦12.9m of personal income tax.

polls.question: On Rev360, which of these can be negotiated?
options: The tax in an assessment, through proper process
polls.why: Penalties and interest are automatic. The assessed tax can be engaged on legally.
